content.endpoint: All Other NVIDIA Container Toolkit Assets

content.description:
**libNVVM API** provides an interface for generating PTX code from both binary and text NVVM IR inputs. Compatible input can be generated by tools and libraries that produce LLVM 7.0 IR and bitcode.

More information: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/libnvvm-api/index.html

**NSIGHT Systems CLI** provides a simple interface to collect on a target without using the GUI. The collected data can then be copied to any system and analyzed later.

The CLI is distributed in the Target directory of the standard Nsight Systems download package.

If you wish to run the CLI without root (recommended mode), you will want to install in a directory where you have full access.

More information: https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-systems/UserGuide/index.html

**In Scope:**
* Security testing for Nsight Systems should be limited to the CUDA Toolkit on x86 desktop platforms.

* Ensure that many Nsight Systems commands, which require super-user privileges, cannot be overridden through privilege escalation during security testing.

**NVIDIA Nsight Developer Tools** are a powerful set of libraries, SDKs, and developer tools spanning across desktop and mobile targets that enable developers to build, debug, profile, and develop software that utilizes the latest accelerated computing hardware.

More information about all dev tools: https://developer.nvidia.com/tools-overview

---

**Scoping focus:**

*Debugger Security:*
Look for Hardware Misconfiguration:
Ensure debuggers do not allow hardware to be put in a bad state.
This is critical in cloud environments to prevent one container from affecting other users or the entire machine.

*Virtualization Security:*
Investigate any actions that could lead to escaping virtualization.
Escaping virtualization can compromise the security of the entire system.

*User Permissions:*
Check that only super users have the rights to control or affect processes belonging to other users.
Related article, see overview point 2: https://developer.nvidia.com/nvidia-development-tools-solutions-err_nvgpuctrperm-permission-issue-performance-counters

*Context Isolation:*
Focus on ensuring that profilers maintain strict context isolation.
Verify that profilers do not interfere with or access other applications during context switches.

Test for vulnerabilities that could allow a profiler to escape its designated context and affect other processes.

By concentrating on these areas, security researchers can help identify and mitigate potential security risks associated with profilers.

**Further resources about specific dev tools**

**CUDA-GDB** is the NVIDIA tool for debugging CUDA applications on Linux and QNX systems.: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-gdb/index.html

**Nsight Compute** is an interactive kernel profiler for CUDA applications. It provides detailed performance metrics and API debugging via a user interface and command line tool.: https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/index.html

**Nsight Eclipse Plugins** offers full-featured IDE that provides an all-in-one integrated environment to edit, build, debug and profile CUDA-C applications.: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/nsightee-plugins-install-guide/index.html

**NVIDIA® Nsight™ Eclipse Edition** is a unified CPU plus GPU integrated development environment (IDE) for developing CUDA® applications on Linux and Mac OS X for the x86, and ARM platforms. It is designed to help developers on all stages of the software development process.: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/nsight-eclipse-plugins-guide/index.html

**Compute Sanitizer** is a functional correctness checking suite included in the CUDA toolkit: https://docs.nvidia.com/compute-sanitizer/ComputeSanitizer/index.html

**The Nsight Systems CLI** provides a simple interface to collect on a target without using the GUI. The collected data can then be copied to any system and analyzed later.: https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-systems/UserGuide/index.html

**NVRTC** is a runtime compilation library for CUDA C++. It accepts CUDA C++ source code in character string form and creates handles that can be used to obtain the PTX. The PTX string generated by NVRTC can be loaded by cuModuleLoadData and cuModuleLoadDataEx, and linked with other modules by using the nvJitLink library or using cuLinkAddData of the CUDA Driver API. This facility can often provide optimizations and performance not possible in a purely offline static compilation.

More information: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/nvrtc/

**Scoping guidance:**
* Only test most CUDA toolkit major/minor release, example: version 13.1. Download link: https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-downloads
* Test nvJPEG most recent version included in CUDA toolkit
* Test nvCOMP most recent version, download link: https://developer.nvidia.com/nvcomp-downloads

**Out of scope:**
All libraries and versions not explicitly mentioned above

Deprecated platforms: maxwell, pascal and volta

**NVCC is the CUDA Compiler Driver**

More information: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-compiler-driver-nvcc/index.html

**nvJitLink** The JIT Link APIs are a set of APIs which can be used at runtime to link together GPU devide code.

More information:  https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/nvjitlink/index.html
